verdict.rationale: Tailscale ships its own Tailscale SSH feature, which manages SSH authentication and authorization inside the tailnet, and MagicDNS hostnames let users SSH to devices by name. That only implies credential-free connection; nothing documents a saved-host list or one-tap connect. A community user also describes Tailscale SSH's browser-based login flow as poor UX, which suggests some interactive re-authentication. missing for 10: saved-host/bookmark UI, one-tap connect, explicit documentation that credentials need not be re-entered, hands-on corroboration of a credential-free reconnect flow.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can connect to a saved host with one tap without re-entering credentials

citations.quote: Use Tailscale SSH to manage the authentication and authorization of SSH connections in your tailnet.
MagicDNS hostnames let them browse http://laptop:8000 or SSH from anywhere.
